req.title: Session cookie has HttpOnly attribute
req.statement: The system shall set HttpOnly on the session cookie.

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that the session cookie must have the HttpOnly attribute set. This is a security feature to prevent client-side scripts from accessing the cookie. The test suite includes a positive test to verify the presence of the HttpOnly attribute, a negative test to check the absence of the attribute, and a boundary test to ensure the attribute is set correctly when a session is created.

tests.name: test_session_cookie_httponly_positive
preconditions: The Flask app is configured for testing.
actions: Create a session by logging in.
expected: The session cookie has the HttpOnly attribute set.
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()
client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'testuser', 'password': 'testpass'})
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'testuser', 'password': 'testpass'})
cookies = r.headers.getlist('Set-Cookie')
assert any('HttpOnly' in cookie for cookie in cookies)

tests.name: test_session_cookie_httponly_negative
preconditions: The Flask app is configured for testing.
actions: Attempt to access a session cookie without logging in.
expected: No session cookie is set, hence no HttpOnly attribute.
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
cookies = r.headers.getlist('Set-Cookie')
assert not any('session=' in cookie for cookie in cookies)
